about: The old Trillion app's features move into the Workshop byte for byte. Groups come from the rows of Trillion's capabilities.json that name moves_to. Engine pieces (sign-in and the door, the stores, the Worker entry) stay: they are ported to Rust, not moved. Provider calls (Durable Object storage, KV, env bindings) are swapped for the records door's calls by the calls rows; a group with a provider call no row swaps is held. The KV rows swap only to calls the records door offers (read and write at @own-records) and need a door the caller hands in; a credential read from an env binding has no call swap, because the door hands credentials by handle through the tool row's invoke.connection, so such a group is held until its row declares that. Groups with no moves_to row are listed by hand in groups. read_as_rows names the opinion content that becomes rows of the person's own lists (imported there separately): a moved logic file that imports one of these is not held for it; the file stays in the source, is not moved, and the logic file reads those rows from its caller once adapted.

not_provider_calls.why: placeCacheFolder(env = process.env) reads the cache folder a computer names in its process environment; it is no Worker binding.

calls.means: A KV read of one JSON entry becomes records:read at @own-records: the record kind is the binding's name, the id the key.
A KV write of one JSON text becomes records:write at @own-records of that value.
A KV delete becomes records:write of null for that id.

groups.capability: set up a new account with your AI: the setup contract as data, run by the existing workflow, with connecting an AI as the entrance, never the finished outcome
tell an AI how to look at what a person is pursuing: where to look and what to do about it
place a person's pursuits on a map of a full life, what they serve and which parts of life they touch, with their own map as a list
